RagShortTexts: In 1259 at Pelagonia, Nicaea routed the Latin-Epirote coalition, capturing Achaea's prince.

Variants.Content: Fought in autumn 1259 on the plains of Pelagonia, this pivotal clash decided the fate of the Byzantine world. Sebastokrator John Palaiologos outmaneuvered a grand anti-Nicaean coalition of Epirus, Sicily, and the Principality of Achaea. Sowing discord among the Greek and Frankish leadership, John crushed the isolated Latin vanguard; Prince William II of Villehardouin was captured hiding in a haystack, yielding fortresses like Mystras that enabled the recapture of Constantinople in 1261.
The capture of the Prince of Achaea broke the spine of Latin crusader hegemony in Greece, opening the Golden Gate to the Palaiologoi.
